messages.subject: Re: DIA-NNtoMSstats
parts:
Dear MSstats Team,

We have been asking for an adapter now also for quite some time and I think that the numbers quite clearly show that DIA-NN is being used more and more:

In 2021 the Nature DIA-NN paper was cited 81 times according to google scholar.
and in 2022 it was cited 227 times
and in 2023 so far it was already cited 66 times suggesting that the number of users quickly increases

Additionally, DIA-NN is a free-to-use software which shows great performance for normal DIA
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36609502/

and for Phospho / PTM:
https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.jproteome.1c00490

We would really appreciate it if the next release of MSstats and MSstatsPTM could contain a supported converter and again I am happy to help if you need any example data / analysis of known datasets with DIA-NN.

Best Klemens

we would love to test the advance methods in MSstats for feature selection and outlier filtering in our large patient cohorts measured in DIA.

We use DIA-NN in our searches.

I wanted to comment in this thread because I have noticed that the DIANNtoMSstats converter is not working.

I have debugged the function and believe to have found the culprit.

It seems the cleanDIANN function is removing everything with an NA from the final DIANN table. 

see line 37 in clean_DIANN function .

I re-wrote the functions locally with this modification and now I get the expected result, based on a DIANN output from ours, version 1.8. 

Sadly I can't promise I would make a pull request in GitHub to collaborate with this modification, because I am short in time. 

Best wishes,
Miguel

Dear MSstats team,

we would love to test the advance methods in MSstats for feature selection and outlier filtering in our large patient cohorts measured in DIA.

We use DIA-NN in our searches.

I wanted to comment in this thread because I have noticed that the DIANNtoMSstats converter is not working.

I have debugged the function and believe to have found the culprit.

It seems the cleanDIANN function is removing everything with an NA from the final DIANN table. 

see line 37 in clean_DIANN function .

I re-wrote the functions locally with this modification and now I get the expected result, based on a DIANN output from ours, version 1.8. 

Sadly I can't promise I would make a pull request in GitHub to collaborate with this modification, because I am short in time. 

Best wishes,
Miguel
